brief.audience: client reviewers opening a private secure portal
brief.visual_target: Apple Liquid Glass-inspired secure access page with official Halo Fire logo and an interactive Three.js halo/flame hero
brief.interaction: hover, click pulse, and drag tug/stretch on the 3D flame material

references_used.purpose: Locked visual rules: one halo only, logo-derived flame, no image plane, Apple-glass login panel, no fake data

references_used.title: Halo Fire Hero Visual Reference Gate
references_used.purpose: Compared rejected browser result, generated flame/halo reference, and official logo before the accepted mesh pass
Actual Halo Fire logo remains deterministic in header/card and supplies the flame silhouette language
Material direction for translucent depth, highlights, hierarchy, and readable glass controls

reject_criteria: No rectangular hero box or visible frame
No clipped halo or clipped flame base
No cartoon yellow core or unrelated abstract VFX
Drag must tug/stretch the flame material, not rotate the display
No hidden draggable logo/image in the hero
No fake metrics, demo data, AHJ/permit overclaims, web-scraping/co-development copy, or internal-alpha wording
Screenshot must exist, decode, and be visually inspected

reasons: Yellow cartoon core did not match the Halo Fire mark
Flame was oversized and not sufficiently logo-derived
Codex in-app browser preview shows one halo, no visible hero box, no clipping, no pasted image plane
Hero is a live Three.js canvas with logo-derived extruded flame mesh, right flame tongue, and bottom cutout
Login copy is clean and contains no fake dashboard data or internal-alpha wording
All logo images are non-draggable; fallback logo opacity is zero after scene readiness
Browser state reported renderer mode webgpu and heroReady true

final_decision: Accepted for this bounded login-page visual slice. Remaining risk: it is a stylized extruded brand flame, not a physically simulated volumetric fire system.
